statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-45491 (GHSA-7q4v-2mr6-5gpx) is a .NET tampering issue in System.Formats.Tar: TarFile.ExtractToDirectory follows a symbolic link in the archive, so a crafted tar file can write files outside the extraction directory. Microsoft lists the .NET 10.0 runtime (Microsoft.NETCore.App.Runtime) as affected on all platforms and architectures from 10.0.0 through 10.0.8 and fixed in 10.0.9 (https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-7q4v-2mr6-5gpx, https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/404, https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/10.0/10.0.9/10.0.9.md). DHI dotnet10-runtime for Alpine 3.23 builds .NET 10 for Linux from Microsoft's source release, and each build's version is the .NET runtime version it carries. Scanned all 264 packages of the twelve published builds (10.0.2-r0, 10.0.3-r0, 10.0.4-r0, 10.0.5-r0, 10.0.6-r0, 10.0.7-r0, 10.0.8-r0, 10.0.9-r0, 10.0.10-r0, 10.0.13-r0, 10.0.14-r0 and 10.0.15-r0) for x86_64 and aarch64, including the files inside the nupkg and other zip archives they hold: every build ships the Microsoft.NETCore.App shared framework, which holds System.Formats.Tar.dll, at its own .NET version, in dotnet10-runtime and in the .NET SDK held by dotnet10-runtime-bootstrap, and the .NET runtime packs at that version in dotnet10-runtime-bootstrap: 10.0.2 to 10.0.8 in the first seven builds and 10.0.9 or later from 10.0.9-r0 on. The range ends at 10.0.9-r0 because it is the first published build with the fix.

CVE-2026-45491 (GHSA-7q4v-2mr6-5gpx) is a .NET tampering issue in System.Formats.Tar: TarFile.ExtractToDirectory follows a symbolic link in the archive, so a crafted tar file can write files outside the extraction directory. Microsoft lists the .NET 8.0 runtime (Microsoft.NETCore.App.Runtime) as affected on all platforms and architectures from 8.0.0 through 8.0.27 and fixed in 8.0.28 (https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-7q4v-2mr6-5gpx, https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/404, https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/8.0/8.0.28/8.0.28.md). DHI dotnet8-runtime for Alpine 3.23 builds .NET 8 for Linux from Microsoft's source release, and each build's version is the .NET runtime version it carries. Scanned all 220 packages of the ten published builds (8.0.23-r0, 8.0.24-r0, 8.0.25-r0, 8.0.26-r0, 8.0.27-r0, 8.0.29-r0, 8.0.31-r0, 8.0.32-r0, 8.0.33-r0 and 8.0.34-r0) for x86_64 and aarch64, including the debug packages and the files inside the nupkg archives they hold: every build ships System.Formats.Tar.dll at its own .NET version in the Microsoft.NETCore.App shared framework of dotnet8-runtime and of the .NET SDK held by dotnet8-runtime-bootstrap, and in that version's runtime pack and NativeAOT compiler pack held by dotnet8-runtime-bootstrap; the other copies are reference assemblies with no implementation code. That version is 8.0.23 to 8.0.27 in the first five builds and 8.0.29 or later from 8.0.29-r0 on (for example, the System.Formats.Tar.dll in dotnet8-runtime has file version 8.0.2726.22922 in 8.0.27-r0 and 8.0.2926.32403 in 8.0.29-r0 on both architectures). No 8.0.28 build was published; the build after 8.0.27-r0 is 8.0.29-r0. The range ends at 8.0.29-r0 because it is the first published build with the fix.
